key_insight: Learnable Subspace Projections jointly learns which weight subspaces to remove end-to-end, avoiding the local compression criteria that fail when errors accumulate across deep models.
engineering_relevance: The method turns frozen pretrained layers into standard low-rank factors and can substantially cut memory, KV-cache size, and inference cost on standard hardware.
method: Assign an orthogonal projector to each linear layer or tied layer group.
Optimize all projectors jointly with a global objective such as KL to the dense model or the original training loss while keeping pretrained weights frozen.
Initialize from whitened SVD truncation and allocate ranks by output KL per parameter saved; merge projectors into low-rank factors after training.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on OPT-125M/1.3B, Qwen3-4B, Llama-2-7B, and ViT-B/16, with LSP outperforming baselines more strongly at higher compression; at -70% compression on Llama-2-7B it reached 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity and 42.2% mean zero-shot accuracy versus 13.3 and 36.0% for the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Training requires optimizing a new set of projectors and careful rank allocation, and the approach relies on a good initialization and the assumption that frozen weights remain adequate after compression.
paper_title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression
